svg.title: Kitchen lighting: 5 V APA102 minimum breadboard layout
svg.desc: Minimum-component experiment with an Arduino Nano 33 IoT and one to five APA102 pixels powered from its USB socket. Close the underside VUSB solder bridge SJ1 to enable USB 5 V at header c12. Feed the left positive rail locally at row 12 and ground at row 14; bridge both left rail midpoint breaks to supply the strip at rows 40 and 43. Nano D13 connects directly to CI and D11 directly to DI at 3.3 V; operation is not guaranteed with every strip. No separate input jack, buffer, resistors or capacitors are fitted. All connecting wires are drawn.
svg.text: Close VUSB solder bridge (SJ1, Nano underside).

g.title: P1: a1 → b41. Nano D13 / SCK → strip CI, direct 3.3 V clock
P2: i2 → b42. Nano D11 / COPI → strip DI, direct 3.3 V data
V0: a12 → L+12. Nano USB-fed 5V / VUSB (c12 row) → left + rail; close SJ1
V1: b43 → L+43. Lower left + rail → strip +5 V
N1: a14 → L-14. Nano GND (c14 row) → left − rail
N2: b40 → L-40. Lower left − rail → strip GND
B1: L+31 → L+34. Bridge left + rail midpoint break
B2: L-31 → L-34. Bridge left − rail midpoint break

svg.text: Direct 3.3 V signals: operation is not guaranteed.
